title: Forensic Rollback Engine with Cost Signal Attenuation and Safe Apply Simulation
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: config changes (autoscale/batching/cache knobs, kernel flags) occasionally cause cost regressions or transient instability. Current reactive rollbacks are manual and slow; safety signals are noisy when traffic patterns shift. Goal: build an automated forensic rollback engine that simulates and stages config applies, uses economic signals to attenuate noisy triggers, and performs safe, reversible rollbacks with state reconciliation across runtime components (serve nodes, KV cache, routing table).
scope: Phase 1 implements offline apply-simulations, live canary apply with staged traffic siphoning, a stability delta score combining latency/error/cost deltas, and a rollback sequencer that reconciles in-flight KV cache state. Does NOT include multi-region cross-account orchestration (Phase 2).
decisions: Use a composite stability delta (latency P95, error rate, per-token cost) rather than single metric thresholds
Simulate config changes in a shadow environment with production traffic replay prior to live canary
Rollback triggers must require both an economic threshold breach and signal persistence for N minutes to avoid flapping
KV cache quarantine: Evict or isolate KV entries mutated by canary replicas to avoid cross-contamination
Make remediation path reversible: keep prior config snapshot and ordering operations idempotent
tasks: Design simulation harness and traffic replay interface (engineering + infra)
Implement stability delta calculator and sliding-window aggregator
Build rollback sequencer with ordered reconciliation steps (config, routing, kv-evict, metrics reset)
Integrate with Console alerting and per-route cost breakdowns
Create canary policy UI knobs (duration, traffic fraction, economic thresholds)
End-to-end tests and chaos scenarios using staging clusters
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting. Aligned on composite stability delta and simulation-first approach.
2026-02-28: Prototype of traffic-replay harness complete; can replay 1m QPS trace to shadow cluster (PR #1423).
2026-03-03: Stability delta v0 implemented in metrics pipeline; tested locally against historic incidents and flagged 3 of 4 regressions.
2026-03-06: Initial KV quarantine design reviewed by storage team; decided on per-canary namespace + soft-evict window.
2026-03-09: Sequencer API contract drafted; integration points with rollout controller identified. Miguel onboarded infra dependencies.
implementation_notes: Sequencer will apply a 3-step reconciler: (1) freeze new partitions and divert canary traffic, (2) reconcile config and kernel flags on nodes in deterministic order, (3) perform kv-cache quarantine/evict and warm caches. Rollback paths will be executed atomically where possible; otherwise use compensating operations with idempotent markers.
testing_plan: Unit tests for stability delta and sim harness, end-to-end in staging with injected cost spikes and latency regressions, canary-to-production shadow run for 48h, chaos tests (node restart, network partition), postmortem validation against two prior incidents (INC-2025-11, INC-2025-27).
risks: False positives from traffic pattern shifts; mitigated by persistence window and economic weighting
KV quarantine complexity could cause cold-cache penalties after rollback
Rollback sequencing may leave transient mismatched states if steps partially fail
mitigations: Introduce graduated rollback: soft-throttle, then full revert; prefer throttles when possible
Add cache-warmup jobs after rollback to reduce cold-start cost impact
Implement idempotent replay and reconciliation checkpoints with clear operator signals
review_feedback: PM (Lena Cho): make economic thresholds customer-configurable per-dedicated pool. Security (Ravi Patel): review KV quarantine and data residency implications. Design (Jin Park): add console UX flows for 'simulate apply' and 'preview cost delta'.
notes: Next steps: finalize sequencer API by 2026-03-15, schedule staging run 2026-03-18. Consider feature flag gating for Dedicated customers first. Keep rollback dry-run logs for 30 days for post-incident analysis.
